dialogue.agent: Hello, how may I help you today?

dialogue.user: Hi! I'm looking to buy a book, but I want to stick to a moderate budget. Could you tell me what options you have available in the $15 to $30 price range?
dialogue.agent:
Here are five highly rated books in your $15–$30 price range:

- **Klingberg Children's Home (CT) (Images of America)** – $21.99, 5.0 stars (1 review): A book on the history of the Klingberg Children's Home, written by someone with deep family ties to the organization.
- **In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod** – $22.24, 5.0 stars (8 reviews): Combines history, literature, and nature, with detailed walking routes and Thoreau-inspired essays about Cape Cod.
- **Tasteful Creations: Original Quilts and Family Recipes** – $19.99, 5.0 stars (1 review): Features family quilt patterns and recipes.
- **Turgenev: Plays** – $22.64, 5.0 stars (1 review): Translations and adaptations of Russian literary plays.
- **Call of the Canyon** – $15.76, 5.0 stars (1 review): No further description available.

Is there a particular genre or topic you’re most interested in? Or would you like more details or reviews for any of these titles?

products.title: Klingberg Children's Home (CT) (Images of America)
products.description: About the Author Mark H. Johnson, a vice president of the Klingberg Family Centers, has both personal and professional ties to the Klingberg Children's Home. In addition to working at the agency for more than twenty-five years, he grew up nearby and knew many of the children at the Klingberg Children's Home. His grandparents worked at the home in the 1920s, and his family has been connected with the organization for decades. The author will donate all royalties from the sale of this book to the Klingberg Family Centers.

products.title: In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod
products.description: Review "A highly original and fascinating walking guide to the Cape, Adam Gamble has done a masterful job of combining history, literature, and outdoor adventure. In the Footsteps of Thoreau is the next best thing to having the 'Traveler from Concord' as our walking companion—a must for any devotee of Cape Cod or Thoreau!"  —Robert Finch, coeditor of the Norton Book of Nature Writing and editor of A Place Apart: A Cape Cod Reader From the Publisher On Cape Publications are dedicated to creating valuable books and publications celebrating Cape Cod, the Islands and the surrounding region. On Cape Publications intend to assist in the appreciation and enjoyment of our shared history, natural environment and community. Please feel free to contact us: Oncapepubs@capecod.net. Thank you for displaying an interest. From the Inside Flap - 25 Historic walking routes, ranging from a quarter of a mile to 14 miles. - 55 fascinating entries on many of the Capes most famous historic sites. - 30 up-to-date, detailed hiking maps across Cape Cod. - 30 Superb illustrations of subjects Henry David Thoreau saw and wrote about while on Cape Cod. - Dozens of inspiring quotes from Thoreau on the Art of Walking. - Informative essays on Thoreau and the 19th Century Cape Cod he loved. - A user-friendly design that makes it easy to tailor this book to your walking needs and preferences. About the Author Adam Gamble is a writer and photographer is the publisher of the regional book company On Cape Publications, where he has edited and overseen the production of dozens of books in a variety of genres. He is the author of A Public Betrayed and authored titles in the Good Night Our World series of boardbooks. Excerpt. © Reprinted by permission. All rights reserved. GETTING STARTED In the Footsteps of Thoreau. Henry David Thoreau was a dedicated walker with an unsurpassed passion for the outdoors. He was a gifted observer of the natural world and an accomplished surveyor who kept detailed records of where he went and what he saw. His nature Classic Cape Cod is widely considered to be the finest book ever written about this part of New England. Who could be a better Cape Cod walking guide and companion than Thoreau himself? In the Footsteps of Thoreau is based on the premise that by better understanding Thoreaus legendary experiences on Cape Cod, our own experiences on this precious peninsula can be greatly enriched. In 1854, one reviewer of Thoreaus recently-published Walden, or Life in the Woods, Wrote: If men were to follow in Mr. Thoreaus steps, by being more obedient to their loftiest instincts, there would, indeed, be a falling off in the splendor of our houses, in the richness of our furniture and dress, in the luxury of our tables, but how poor are these things in comparison with the new grandeur and beauty which would appear in the souls of men... Such is the spirit in which In the footsteps of Thoreau has been Written nearly a century and a half later. All of the routes in this guide are based on Thoreaus actual walks as recorded in Cape Cod and Thoreaus Journal. They have been selected with the aid of 19th-Century maps of the area, Thoreaus own hand-made maps of the Cape, recent topographical maps, aerial photographs and a great deal of legwork in the field. In addition to the twenty-five walks in this book, the sites section includes fifty-five roads, rivers, lighthouses, windmills and other historic sites, most of which Thoreau wrote about and can still be visited today. Furthermore, this book features many illustrations of places, plants, and animals encountered by Thoreau that are still found on the Cape. Quotations are also used throughout this book as examples of what Thoreau though while he was here, and to serve as inspirations for each walkers own adventures. It should be emphasized that In the Footsteps of Thoreau was not conceived to help walkers imitate Thoreau or to re-enact his Cape Cod experiences. This book is designed as a tool to provide a new approach for understanding one of Americas greatest writers, and to assist walkers in discovering the many wonders of Cape Cod for themselves. Thoreau once wrote: I desire that there be as many different persons in the world as possible; but I would have each one be very careful to find out and pursue his own way and not his fathers or mothers or his neighbors instead With this in mind, it is hoped that those who follow In the footsteps of Thoreau will come away with an enhanced appreciation of not only Thoreaus Cape Cod, but their own Cape Cod. dialogue.user: Thanks for these options! Out of curiosity, can you tell me a bit more about "Call of the Canyon"? Specifically, what genre does it fall under and what is the general storyline or subject of the book?
dialogue.agent:
"**Call of the Canyon**" ($15.76, 5.0 stars, 1 review) is the second book in the Waiting for Dusk series, and it blends elements of romance, drama, and time travel. The story follows Kate Roberts and Drew Kelly as they face new challenges when Drew joins Kate in the present. The synopsis hints at romantic tension, dramatic events (including a wedding, tragic accident, and family scandal), and conflicts that impact both the past and present.

If you enjoy character-driven stories with romance and a touch of time travel drama, this could be a good fit. Would you like to hear what readers are saying about it, or would you like more options?

result.title: Call of the Canyon
result.features: Two Lives... Two Worlds... Heartbreak awaits. Call of the Canyon, second of the Waiting for Dusk series, continues the dramatic story of Kate Roberts and Drew Kelly. New challenges face the couple when Drew joins Kate in the present. Nothing is easy. Tyson’s still their nemesis, causing trouble whenever he can. Carl, Kate’s friend and neighbor, moves back home to Ohio and creates unexpected problems at the canyon. A wedding, a tragic accident, and a family broken by scandal affect both the past and present. And in the end, Kate may pay the ultimate price.

dialogue.user:
Thanks for the description! I’m not too concerned about what reviewers say, but I do appreciate that it hits romance and time travel elements. 

Before I decide, could you give me some details on “In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod”? I’m curious what the style and main focus are—is it mostly a guidebook, more of a narrative, or something else?
dialogue.agent:
"In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod" ($22.24, 5.0 stars, 8 reviews) is a blend of hiking guide, historical reference, and literary appreciation. It's practical for planning nature walks—offering 25 mapped routes (from 0.25 to 14 miles), entries on Cape Cod’s famous historic sites, and detailed hiking maps. The book also weaves in numerous quotes from Thoreau, essays about his connection to 19th-century Cape Cod, and illustrations of the region and its nature.

In terms of style, it’s part guidebook, part celebration of Thoreau’s literary legacy and philosophy, and part local history. If you appreciate outdoor adventure, history, or Thoreau himself, it serves as both a reference and a narrative companion. Would you like to make a decision or learn about other titles?

That sounds pretty unique—a mix of outdoor guide and literary content is interesting. Just to clarify, both “In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod” and “Call of the Canyon” are within my budget, and both have a 5.0 star rating, right? 

Also, could you tell me if “Call of the Canyon” is suitable to read without having read the first book in the Waiting for Dusk series? I don’t want to start in the middle if it’s going to be confusing.
dialogue.agent:
Yes, both “In the Footsteps of Thoreau: 25 Historic & Nature Walks on Cape Cod” ($22.24, 5.0 stars, 8 reviews) and “Call of the Canyon” ($15.76, 5.0 stars, 1 review) are within your stated budget and have excellent customer ratings.

Regarding “Call of the Canyon,” a reader review makes it clear that this book is the second in the Waiting for Dusk series and that the story is “somewhat complicated”—the reviewer suggests you need to pay attention to what’s happening. This implies the book may be best enjoyed if you've read the first in the series, as it continues the ongoing story and character development.

Would you like to proceed with one of these, or do you want recommendations that are standalone reads?

top_reviews.title: A page turner!
top_reviews.text: The second book in this series continues to pull you in to the time travel adventures of the family and friends of Kate. Pennick deals with the issues of young adults while exploring time travel. The story is somewhat complicated- you need to pay attention to what's happening. I'm looking forward to the next book in this series.

top_reviews.title: Awesome Cape Cod Journey
top_reviews.text: I live on Cape Cod and have been working my way through Thoreau's footsteps chapter by chapter - what a fun time and an absolutely fascinating read. Thank you Adam, you have captured the Cape in a way most visitors and locals only dream of experiencing.

top_reviews.title: Wonderful Book
top_reviews.text: Many people come to Cape Cod every summer, but so few know much about the cape.  I'd recommend that if you're one of the many people who rent a Cape house in the summer... bring this book along with you.  You'll love it and you'll see the Cape differently and perhaps... find yourself walking in the footsteps of Thoreau.
